sourceObservations.observations: Title identifies Lecture 29, Introduction to Decision Trees and Random Forests, printed page 1.

Objectives list root/internal/leaf/branch anatomy, classification versus regression, example, pre/post pruning, forest introduction, two randomization mechanisms and code workflow. No new formal algorithm claim.
Contents roadmap for tree anatomy, tasks, examples, pruning, logic rules, strengths/weaknesses, then forest construction and parameters. No independent technical premise.

Decision trees are supervised, used for classification and regression, recursively splitting feature tests into subsets until pure or a stopping rule. Four-animal tree: Has feathers? true ->Can fly? true Hawk/false Penguin; feathers false ->Has fins? true Dolphin/false Bear. This is a closed four-animal taxonomy, not a universal biology classifier. The displayed mglearn call plots the illustration rather than fitting data.

Root receives all training samples and applies the first split. Branches represent discrete test outcomes, internal nodes further split data. Schematic shows root plus three additional decision boxes, but not all leaves are drawn as boxes. Root is also an internal node when it splits; the informal intermediate-level wording should not exclude it generally.

Actual pixels: local test f_m(x); numeric x_j > omega_m yields binary axis-parallel decision. Categorical equality color==red is itself binary, whereas a general categorical split can branch once per category. Do not conflate these claims.

Single-feature tests yield axis-parallel splits; multivariate weighted linear sum w_j x_j+b >0 yields oblique hyperplane. Classification impurity and regression MSE distinguish split objectives. Multivariate is not necessarily nonlinear.

Terminal leaves have no children; classification majority class, squared-error regression mean target, not mean feature vector. Diagram has 4 internal nodes, 5 leaves, 9 nodes, 8 edges and maximum depth 3 edges; leaves are not all at identical depth.

Univariate regions hyperrectangles; linear multivariate regions polyhedra. Pure node means identical training class, not guarantee of generalization. Stop by depth, counts or impurity improvement. Diagram partitions y=2.5 first, then x=4.5 only below; lower-left 4 blue, lower-right 1 red, upper 4 red and 2 blue, so upper remains impure.

Hierarchical divide-and-conquer applies to both target types. Classification uses majority leaf/minimum impurity; ordinary squared-error regression uses mean target and MSE/variance reduction. This is criterion-specific rather than every possible regression tree.

Humanoid example inputs Acc_Z vertical acceleration and Gyro_X pitch rate under source naming, target stable0/forward1/backward2. Axis naming is an example convention, not universal. Interpretable if-else motivation does not prove all trees faster than all NNs/SVMs; image rectangle is blank.

Actual code imports numpy, pyplot; sklearn.tree DecisionTreeClassifier and plot_tree; sklearn.inspection DecisionBoundaryDisplay; model_selection train_test_split; matplotlib.colors ListedColormap. Boundary display visualization not training and discrete colors map classes.

Seed42,N150. Normal means stable[9.8,0], forward[4,150], backward[4,-150], standard deviations stable[0.5,10], falls[2,30]; each(N,2). Vertical stack yields450x2, labels contiguous150 each0,1,2. Scale means standard deviation, not variance. Synthetic generated examples not measured real fall validation.
Flowchart splits dataset train/test; training arrow enters tree, final prediction exits. Test is not shown fitting tree. 4 internal nodes and5 leaf nodes schematic, same unbalanced topology as p863.

Prepruning stops growth by depth, leaf sample minimum and leaf count. Source min_samples_leaf wording incorrectly suggests parent-count split test: actual constraint is both resulting leaves. Postpruning description is reduced-error pruning using pruning set, not all pruning algorithms. Printed claim sklearn only preprunes is outdated/false for modern ccp_alpha cost-complexity pruning. Pure full leaves may be impossible with contradictory identical inputs.

train_test_split test_size0.3,stratify=y,random_state42 ->315 training,135test with105/45 each class. max_depth3 is upper bound on three edges/questions, not exactly three actual levels. fit(X_tr,y_tr) only. Root depthzero.

Feature map x Acc_Z,y Gyro_X; red forward upper band,blue stablemiddle,greenbackwardlower. Horizontal thresholds around61.1 and-45.45 depend on Gyro_X only in this fitted example. Background predictions not true physical stability guarantee or evidence that acceleration never matters.

Exact printed tests Gyro_X<=-45.452 ->backward; else <=61.097 ->stable;elseforward. Countsroot315[105,105,105],right210[105,105,0],threepureleaves105each. Printed classStable at root/right is tie-breaking not strict majority. Five nodes,threeleaves,depth2edges despite maxdepth3.

Strength visualization and threshold-order scaling invariance under positive rescaling in exact arithmetic; not arbitrary transforms/rounding. Weakness overfit and data instability. Extrapolation wording misleading: ordinary constant-leaf regressors predict outside feature range but output remains leaf means within target range, not necessarily last training value.

Random forests aggregate multiple randomized trees to reduce variance/overfitting; no guarantee unique tree every draw or universally superior accuracy. Averaging helpful when constituent errors not perfectly correlated.

Bootstrap draws n samples with replacement from n original rows; draws preserve size but duplicates and omissions. Display [2,5,3,2,5] omits1,4;[3,1,1,4,3]omits2,5. Rough one-third missing is expected asymptotic about36.8%, not deterministic nor exact for n5.

At each node choose random candidate feature subset then optimize split among it; max_features controls subset size. Subset resampled per node, not one permanent subset per tree; randomness is not arbitrary threshold choice in standard forest.

Bootstrap and node feature sampling promote diversity, not mathematical guarantee distinct trees. Regression averages scalar predictions; classification averages per-class probability vectors then argmax (soft voting). Majority of hard class labels need not agree.

Forest flowchart uses original training subset for each bootstrap; test set separate. Independent tree predictions aggregated into final prediction, not sequential boosting residual updates. Drawn tree shapes schematic not proof identical learnt structures.

RandomForestClassifier imported sklearn.ensemble; n_estimators5,random_state2,fit training features/labels. max_features sqrt stated alongside both estimator classes is classifier-specific modern default; regressor default differs. Five means count not depth or classes.

Actual panels tree0..4 plus random forest aggregated probability boundary. Axis-aligned constituent bands differ, forest boundary blends predictions but remains piecewise regions; no smooth analytical curve guaranteed. No exact coordinate axis values or accuracy metric printed, so cannot infer exact thresholds or universal superiority.

n_estimators count and compute/memory tradeoff; more trees reduce averaging variance, no strict guaranteed accuracy gain. max_features all eliminates feature-subset exclusion but not bootstrap/tie randomness. Printed regression default log2 is wrong for modern sklearn default1.0; classifier sqrt. Near-always performance statement empirical heuristic not theorem.

Forest scaling robustness, independent-tree parallelization via n_jobs. More memory/can slower than linear model. High-dimensional weakness depends data sparsity/relevance not universal impossibility. Ordinary leaf-mean regression cannot extend numeric target trends beyond training target range but can evaluate unseen feature ranges.

Summary recaps pruning, bootstrap and feature subsets, applications terrain/faults/UAV/defects, DTprototype/RFproduction heuristic. Claim outperforms single DT on all robotics benchmarks unsupported universal. This summary has application facts not merely ornamental.
References only: Muller/Guido,Alpaydin; official sklearn tree and RandomForestClassifier URLs. No new assessable tree claim.
Thank-you only; no examinable content.

independentAnswers.reasoning: Classification target is a category; regression target is numeric. Both are supervised.
Feathers true selects the left flying test; cannot fly false reaches Penguin.
The root selects one subtree; only its one remaining test is needed, not the other subtree test.
All training rows reach root initially; held-out test rows are not fitted.
The strict comparison 4.5>4.5 is false, so no separate equality branch.
Equality red has two outcomes; a multiway category-valued test is a different branching function.
Univariate describes one node test, not a requirement that the entire tree use one feature.
2x1+3x2=6 has nonzero coefficients on both axes and is oblique; single-axis thresholds are not.
Greedy best-at-node optimizes a local criterion, not all possible full tree structures.
Four internal plus five terminal nodes is nine; a connected acyclic tree has nine minus one edges.
Actual leaves occur after two and three edges; terminality does not mean maximum-depth-only.
Minimizing sum(y-c)^2 gives 2(3c-15)=0, so c=5, not median4 or sum15.
Residuals 2-5=-3,4-5=-1,9-5=4; squared sum9+1+16=26 and mean26/3.
2>2.5 false,3>4.5 false: lower-left region.
Upper has four red and two blue; lower-left four blue and lower-right one red are pure.
Intersecting axis-parallel half-spaces gives rectangles or higher-dimensional boxes, possibly unbounded.
Stopping constraints can end at a mixed-label leaf; multiple rows alone do not imply impurity.
Classification impurity yields category prediction; squared-error regression constant is target mean.
The source specifies two sensor inputs and three state category outputs, not numeric-rate targets.
Interpretability of this synthetic example does not establish real-robot safety or comparative speed guarantees.
DecisionTreeClassifier fits; the other named imports visualize or supply plotting colors.
Three150x2 blocks stacked vertically yield450x2.
The second normal argument is scale, a per-feature standard deviation, not variance.
Block labels must match contiguous class blocks, so 150zeros then150ones then150twos.
Gaussian means/spreads are not support bounds; seed changes reproducibility, not measurement provenance.
Learn splits and leaf outputs on training rows; final held-out evaluation uses test rows.
Pre-pruning limits growth while fitting; post-pruning replaces/removes parts after growing.
Official DecisionTreeClassifier API describes ccp_alpha minimal-cost-complexity pruning; plotting and random seeds are not penalties.
The smaller child has2<3; both children must satisfy min_samples_leaf, not merely parent or larger child.
0.3*150=45 per class,135 total; training105 per class.
Stratification preserves target proportions subject to integer sample counts, not feature scaling or accuracy.
Depth limit3 permits actualdepth2; rootdepth0 and growth can stop at pure leaves.
Both thresholds use the vertical Gyro_X coordinate, hence horizontal boundaries.
80 exceeds both -45.452 and 61.097, so two false branches reach Fall_Fwd.
At the explicitly exact rounded threshold, the less-than-or-equal comparison is true, so Fall_Bwd.
105=105=105, so no strict majority. Stable is one deterministic tie-selected class.
Two test boxes and three pure leaves: five total nodes.
Each root class fraction1/3;1-3*(1/3)^2=2/3.
For a>0, x<=t iff ax+b<=at+b; exact ordering preserved, not a Euclidean distance claim.
An unseen input still routes to a terminal mean; constant leaves do not extend an unbounded numeric trend.
Small data perturbation can alter root split and descendants: statistical high variance, not spontaneous mutation.
Averaging diverse trees reduces sensitivity/variance; identical predictions or zero error are not guaranteed.
n draws with replacement from training rows may repeat/omit identities; not sampling without replacement.
Selected distinct identities are2,3,5; complement in1..5 is1,4.
Each draw misses a given row with probability4/5; independence gives(4/5)^5=0.32768.
The omission probability (1-1/n)^n tends to exp(-1); realized omission counts still vary between bootstraps.
The feature candidate set is redrawn at each split node, not once per forest.
Randomizing candidates does not remove optimizing the split criterion within that candidate set.
The equally weighted prediction is (2+5+8)/3 = 5, not the sum or one extreme.
Mean A probability is 1.03/3 = 0.343333; mean B is 1.97/3 = 0.656667. Soft voting predicts B despite the two hard A votes.
Finite random choices can repeat; diversity is encouraged, not guaranteed distinct functions or label sets.
Bootstrap trees fitted separately then aggregated differ from sequential residual-target fitting.
n_estimators=5 means five trees, not classes, features or seed.
random_state=2 fixes pseudo-random choices under unchanged inputs and software; it is not a count or depth parameter.
The snippet needs definitions for X_train and y_train; the earlier code uses different names X_tr and y_tr. Arrays are supported and fitting does not require test labels.
The forest figure shows two classes, circles and triangles. The earlier fall experiment has three classes, so the figure is not evidence of the identical experiment.
The five actual panels show different partitions; the forest combines their predictions. No universal accuracy guarantee follows.
More trees consume computation and storage and may stabilize aggregation; a finite test score need not improve monotonically.
With every feature eligible, bootstrap=True still permits different randomly selected training rows.
The current official regressor default max_features=1.0 uses all features; the classifier default is sqrt. log2 is an available setting, not that regressor default.
The nominal counts are sqrt(9)=3 and 1.0 times 9=9. A float fraction 1.0 is distinct from integer 1.
n_jobs controls parallel worker jobs; n_estimators controls the number of trees.
Scale invariance does not make malformed arrays or raw text automatically suitable model inputs.
Memory and prediction work depend on tree count and depth, so the comparison with a linear model is qualified.
Every mean of targets in [2,8] remains in [2,8]. Averaging those tree means retains the same bound even outside the observed input range.
One example and general aggregation arguments do not establish performance on every robotics benchmark.
Choose between models using held-out performance, latency, memory and interpretability, not an automatic production rule.
A labeled terrain category is a supervised classification target. Continuous force is regression; unlabeled groups are clustering; reward-driven action learning is reinforcement learning.
The source call displays the illustrative animal tree, rather than fitting or validating the later fall-state data.
Eight blue observations among ten give majority blue and empirical probabilities 0.8 blue, 0.2 red.
Perfect accuracy on this synthetic held-out split only establishes that bounded result. Real-world distribution shift and robot safety are not resolved.
